cues.text: Section thirteen: the learning outcome checklist.
This checklist lines up each official learning outcome with the sections of the guide that cover it, so you can check your preparation against what the course expects.
Let us go through the table row by row.
First, the official outcome: define and contextualise IT management principles.
The guide covers this in Sections 1 to 3.
Second, the official outcome: explain IT in organisational structures.
The guide covers this in Section 6.
Third, the official outcome: trace enterprise IT evolution.
The guide covers this in Sections 7 and 8.
Fourth, the official outcome: analyse African and global applications.
The guide covers this in Sections 4 and 5, then Section 8, and then Section 11.
Fifth, the official outcome: apply principles and recommend improvements.
The guide covers this in Sections 2 and 3, and then Sections 9 to 11.
Notice that some sections appear against more than one outcome.
Sections 2 and 3 support both the definition of principles and their application, and Section 8 supports both tracing enterprise IT evolution and analysing African and global applications.
Next, there is some additional scope beyond the official outcomes.
The textbook adds project management, including Waterfall, Agile and Scrum, and this is covered in Section 9.
The applied scope from the LMS adds the CMDB and Shadow IT, and these are covered in Section 10.
Finally, a note on the glossary.
Glossary terms are integrated throughout the guide rather than being duplicated in a separate dictionary.
So when you want to revise a term, look for it in the section where it naturally arises.
